      <h1 id="h-name"><span class="first">Honglin</span> Li</h1>
      <p class="about-desc"><span class="segs"><span class="seg">Postdoctoral Fellow</span> <span class="seg">Electrical and Computer Engineering</span> <span class="seg"><a href="https://www.k-state.edu/">Kansas State University</a></span></span></p>

    <div class="about-bio">
      <p>I am an energy systems researcher and a Postdoctoral Fellow in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
        at Kansas State University. I build optimization and techno-economic models for the design, operation and long-term
        planning of low-carbon energy systems, from hydrogen-integrated renewables and nuclear plants to firm power for AI data
        centers. My current research focuses on firm, low-carbon power for large and fast-growing electricity loads such as
        AI data centers, including small modular reactors.</p>
      <p>My methods include linear, mixed-integer, nonlinear, stochastic and multi-objective optimization, combined with life
        cycle cost and carbon footprint analysis, simulation and reliability modeling. Applications span wind, solar and
        hydrogen systems, regional hydrogen networks, nuclear–hydrogen integration, small modular reactors for data centers,
        grid integration of data centers, and energy storage. My first-author papers appear in <em>Nature Communications</em>,
        <em>Cell Reports Sustainability</em> and the <em>International Journal of Hydrogen Energy</em>.</p>
    </div>
